chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih (may God be pleased with him) narrated from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mus'ada ibn Sadaqah, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them), who said:

Do not greet the Jews, nor the Christians, nor the Magians, nor the idol-worshippers, nor those sitting at tables where wine is served, nor the chess and backgammon players, nor the effeminate men, nor the poet who accuses chaste women of adultery, nor the one who is praying, because the one who is praying cannot return the greeting, as greeting is voluntary for the greeter while returning it is obligatory, nor those who devour usury, nor a man sitting on excrement, nor the one in the bathroom, nor the openly corrupt sinner.

key_terms.الرَّدُّ: The act of returning the greeting

ai.seo_question: Who are the specific people and states mentioned in Shia hadith with whom one should not greet?
ai.summary: Compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Al-Khisal*, this hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq delineates the etiquette of *as-salam* by distinguishing between voluntary greetings and obligatory responses. It categorically excludes non-Muslims, idolaters, and those in states of ritual impurity or distraction, while also noting the 'openly sinful' (*fasiq*) as a distinct group whose greeting may be withheld due to their deviation from piety. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the spiritual and social status of the recipient when offering the greeting of peace.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 12-58 Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his uncle Muhammad ibn Abil Qasim quoted Harun ibn Muslim, on the authority of Mus’adat ibn Sadaqah, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad As-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), “

You should not greet the Jews; the Christians; the Magians ; the idol-worshippers; those sitting at a table on which wine is served; chess players; backgammon players; the effeminates ; poets who accuse chaste women of adultery; those busy praying since they cannot greet you back as greeting is recommendable while greeting back is obligatory; those who devour usury; those who are in the toilet; those who are in the bathroom; and those who are corrupt in the publics eyes.”
